Docker

Package an application with a repeatable runtime.

DOfficial product ↗Open in the hierarchy →
Level 4Inspect the detail

Docker packages application code and runtime dependencies into container images. We can use it to make a website backend, worker, or custom integration easier to run across development and supported hosting environments. A container is one part of delivery: configuration, persistent storage, networking, health checks, and release ownership still need a deliberate operational plan.

Useful outputs

  • Versioned Dockerfile and container image
  • Documented run and configuration instructions
  • Health-check and deployment configuration

Where we can apply it

  • Backend release: source commit → image build → health-checked deployment.
  • Developer setup: repository → local containers → repeatable integration checks.
  • Worker delivery: processing script → runtime image → scheduled or queued execution.
01

Use case 1

Package a backend service so its runtime is consistent across environments.

02

Use case 2

Run local application dependencies for repeatable development setup.

03

Use case 3

Create versioned deployment images for APIs, workers, or data processors.

Inputs we need

  • Application source and runtime requirements
  • Build commands and expected service port
  • Storage, environment, and hosting constraints

Delivery sequence

  • Define a minimal image with the dependencies the service needs.
  • Separate runtime configuration and persistent data from the image.
  • Test startup, health behavior, and the intended deployment environment.

Expert review points

  • Check image contents for unnecessary files and secrets.
  • Review permissions, persistent storage, and resource limits.
